        "contents": "# Building on Windows 11\n\n## Common Issues and Solutions\n\n### Symlink Permission Errors\n\nIf you encounter errors like:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nERROR: Cannot create symbolic link : A required privilege is not held by the client.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Solution 1: Enable Developer Mode (Recommended)**\n1. Press &#96;Win + I&#96; to open Settings\n2. Go to **Privacy &amp; Security** → **For developers**\n3. Toggle **Developer Mode** to **On**\n4. Restart your terminal/PowerShell\n5. Run &#96;npm run package&#96; again\n\n**Solution 2: Run as Administrator**\n- Right-click PowerShell → **Run as administrator**\n- Navigate to project directory\n- Run &#96;npm run package&#96;\n\n### Current Configuration\n\nThe &#96;package.json&#96; is configured with:\n- &#96;forceCodeSigning: false&#96; - Disables code signing\n- &#96;CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false&#96; - Prevents certificate auto-discovery\n- &#96;ELECTRON_BUILDER_CACHE=./cache&#96; - Uses local cache directory\n\nThis configuration should work without Developer Mode, but enabling Developer Mode is the most reliable solution.\n\n### Build Command\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm run package\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis will:\n1.         "contents": "These commands are used to create the final production version of the application, ready for distribution.\n\n3.1 Build Renderer (React) for Production\nThis step compiles your React application into optimized, production-ready assets (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) and typically places them in a dist folder.\n\nCommand\tAction\nnpm run build-renderer\tExecutes webpack in production mode.\n\nExport to Sheets\n\n3.2 Package the Application (Executable/Installer)\nThis is the final step, which runs the production build and then uses Electron Builder to package the app for your target operating system (e.g., creating a .exe installer for Windows).\n\nCommand\tAction\nnpm run package\tRuns build-renderer, then executes electron-builder.\n\nExport to Sheets\n\nOutput Location:\n\nPackaged installers and binaries will be output to the release directory, as defined in the package.json configuration.\n\n4.         "contents": "# 💻 New Development and Build Workflow\n\n\n\n## 1. Development (npm run dev)\nThis is your new development command.\n\n&#96;npm run watch&#96; (in concurrently) starts Webpack in watch mode, compiling your React code and updating the dist folder whenever you save a file.\n\n&#96;npm run electron&#96; uses wait-on to ensure the Webpack build finishes before launching Electron.\n\nCommand: \n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm run dev\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## 2. Building the Renderer (npm run build-renderer)\nThis compiles your React application for production into the dist folder.\n\nCommand: \n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm run build-renderer\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## 3. Packaging the Application (npm run build or npm run package-win)\nThis uses electron-builder to create a final, installable application.\n\n&#96;npm run build-renderer&#96; ensures the latest production React code is bundled.\n\nelectron-builder then takes the compiled files (&#96;dist/**/*&#96; and the main process file) and packages them into an executable.\n\nCommand: \n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm run build # (This runs npm run package-win for convenience)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\Devel-instructions.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {},
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 46
          }
        },
        "contents": "📝 Development Workflow Documentation: Translator &amp; Rewriter\nThis document outlines the standard procedures and commands for developing, running, and packaging the Translator &amp; Rewriter desktop application, which is built using Electron, React, and Webpack.\n\n1. Prerequisites and Setup\nBefore starting development, ensure you have the necessary tools installed and project dependencies handled.\n\nNode.js (LTS): Installed on your system.\n\nGit: Installed for version control.\n\nCode Editor: Visual Studio Code (VS Code) is recommended.\n\nInstall Dependencies: Run the following command in the project root after cloning or creating the directory to install all packages listed in package.json:\n\nBash\n\nnpm install\n2. Core Development Commands\nThe following commands are used during active development and utilize a concurrent setup to manage both the React front-end and the Electron desktop process simultaneously.\n\n2.1 Start Development Mode\nThis is the primary command for development. It automatically starts the Webpack development server and then launches the Electron application, providing live-reloading for your React code.\n\nCommand\tAction\nnpm run dev\tRuns the watch and electron scripts concurrently.\n\nExport to Sheets\n\nUnder the Hood:\n\nnpm run watch: Starts the Webpack dev server, which compiles and serves your React components, typically on http://localhost:8080.\n\nnpm run electron: Uses wait-on to pause until the Webpack server is ready, then launches the Electron main process, which loads the React content into the window.\n\n2.2 Run Electron (Main Process Only)\nThis command is typically used for testing the Electron process directly, often after a production build, or for debugging the main process without the Webpack dev server running.\n\nCommand\tAction\nnpm run start\tDirectly executes the Electron main script (src/main/main.js).\n\nExport to Sheets\n\n3. Building and Packaging\nThese commands are used to create the final production version of the application, ready for distribution.\n\n3.1 Build Renderer (React) for Production",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\src\\main\\preload.js",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {},
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 69
          }
        },
        "contents": "// See the Electron documentation for details on how to use preload scripts:\n// https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/process-model#preload-scripts\n\n// All of the Node.js APIs are available in the preload process.\n// It has the same sandbox as a Chrome extension.\nconst { contextBridge, ipcRenderer } = require('electron');\nconst fs = require('fs');\nconst path = require('path');\n\nconst api = {\n  readConfig: () =&gt; {\n    try {\n      // Look for config.json in multiple locations to be robust\n      const pathsToCheck = [\n        // Development path relative to this file (src/main/preload.js -&gt; root/config.json)\n        path.join(__dirname, '../../config.json'),\n        // Current working directory\n        path.resolve('config.json'),\n        // Parent of CWD (sometimes useful)\n        path.resolve('../config.json')\n      ];\n\n      let configPath = null;\n      for (const p of pathsToCheck) {\n        if (fs.existsSync(p)) {\n          configPath = p;\n          break;\n        }\n      }\n\n      if (configPath) {\n        console.log(&#96;Loading config from: ${configPath}&#96;);\n        const data = fs.readFileSync(configPath, 'utf8');\n        return JSON.parse(data);\n      } else {\n        console.error('Config file not found. Checked paths:', pathsToCheck);\n      }\n    } catch (e) {\n      console.error('Failed to read config file', e);\n    }\n    return null;\n  },\n  openSettings: () =&gt; ipcRenderer.send('open-settings'),\n  notifySettingsUpdated: () =&gt; ipcRenderer.send('settings-updated'),\n  onSettingsUpdated: (callback) =&gt; ipcRenderer.on('settings-updated', callback)\n};\n\ntry {\n  contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('electronAPI', api);\n} catch (e) {\n  // If contextIsolation is disabled, contextBridge might fail or not work as expected\n  // Fallback to direct assignment\n  window.electronAPI = api;\n}\n\n// Ensure it's available in non-isolated contexts if contextBridge didn't throw but didn't work (common in some electron configs)\nif (!window.electronAPI) {\n  window.electronAPI = api;\n}\n\nwindow.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded',",
